items.title: CVE-2026-109618 Impact of Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) on Palo Alto Networks Products  (Severity: CRITICAL)
items.one_liner: Active exploitation of critical PHP RCE vulnerabilities targets internet-exposed Palo Alto Networks management interfaces.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has evaluated its product portfolio regarding two critical PHP remote code execution vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which affect PAN-OS software on PA-Series, VM-Series firewalls, and Panorama. CVE-2026-109618 allows RCE via uninitialized request memory after out-of-memory errors handled by longjmp(), while CVE-2026-109619 leaves global memory pointing to freed memory regions. Active exploitation has been observed against management interfaces exposed to the internet, prompting the vendor to assign a critical CVSS score of 9.2 and recommend restricting management access or deploying virtual patches.
key_facts: CVE-2026-109618: CVSS 9.2, remote code execution via OOM longjmp
CVE-2026-109619: remote code execution via global memory pointing to freed regions
items.bottom_line: Administrators must restrict external access to firewall management interfaces immediately to mitigate actively exploited critical PHP vulnerabilities.

items.one_liner: GitLab released critical patches for multiple high-severity vulnerabilities, including an RCE-capable integer overflow and authentication bypasses.

The updates fix issues including an integer overflow in the regular expression compiler, improper authentication in OmniAuth-to-LDAP lookups, and cache poisoning in OAuth/OIDC endpoints. items.title: NoisyTCP bug gives Linux servers a remote crash problem 11 years in the making
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-99288 (NoisyTCP) is an 11-year-old Linux kernel use-after-free flaw allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to crash servers.
items.summary: Security researcher Hyunwoo Kim has uncovered a remote denial-of-service vulnerability in the Linux kernel tracked as CVE-2026-99288 and dubbed NoisyTCP. Dating back to October 2015, the flaw exists in Linux TCP networking code where separate kernel components conflict while processing incoming traffic, resulting in a use-after-free condition that triggers kernel panics and system crashes. Attackers require no credentials or authentication, only access to an open TCP port on a system processing incoming packets across multiple receive queues. Red Hat rated the vulnerability Important with a CVSS score of 7.5, and patches were committed to the upstream kernel on November 3.
items.bottom_line: CVE-2026-99288 allows unauthenticated attackers to remotely crash Linux servers via a TCP use-after-free vulnerability.

items.title: Criminals are using ARTEX AI agents to speed up cyberattacks, FBI warns
items.one_liner: The FBI warns that threat actors are abusing ARTEX AI penetration-testing agents to achieve privileged access in under three hours.
items.summary: The FBI issued a FLASH advisory warning that cybercriminals are weaponizing ARTEX—an open-source penetration-testing framework—to automate network intrusions and accelerate attacks. Designed to leverage external large language models, ARTEX splits security testing objectives into automated planning tasks, allowing operators to move from target selection to privileged access in under three hours. The tool has been observed targeting sectors including finance, government, healthcare, and technology, leaving defenders minimal window to investigate and mitigate threats.

items.summary: A remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability has been disclosed in the Philips Hue Bridge, affecting the HomeKit Accessory Protocol (HAP) service. items.title: German Military Grounds Quantum Systems Drones Following Reported Cyberattack
items.one_liner: A supply chain attack compromised Quantum Systems' drone control software via a malicious update, forcing the German military to ground its reconnaissance units.
items.summary: German defense drone manufacturer Quantum Systems confirmed a cyberattack occurring in late October 2026 that disrupted operations and triggered an unexpected software update. Domestic intelligence agencies, military counterintelligence, and the federal cybersecurity agency BSI are actively investigating the supply chain compromise.

items.title: Google Project Zero Slashes Bug Disclosure Deadlines, Splitting Experts
items.one_liner: Project Zero's shift to a 30-day disclosure deadline means faster public exposure for exploited CVEs, compressing your patching windows.
items.summary: Google's Project Zero has announced plans to reduce its public disclosure timelines for vendors from 120 days down to 30 days over the course of the next 14 months. The tighter deadline puts immediate pressure on software maintainers to address vulnerabilities much faster than before. items.title: Windows 11 “SignDrop” Zero-Day Exploit Turns Microsoft’s Own Security Fix Against Itself, Grants SYSTEM Privileges
items.one_liner: A Windows zero-day in the CLFS driver allows privilege escalation by weaponizing the very security mechanism designed to protect log integrity.
items.summary: A new zero-day vulnerability dubbed 'SignDrop' has been disclosed, affecting the Windows Common Log File System (CLFS) driver. The exploit allows standard users to escalate privileges to SYSTEM by manipulating the authentication mechanism intended to secure log files. Researcher Abdelhamid Naceri demonstrated that the vulnerability can be triggered by forcing privileged processes, such as Microsoft Defender, to interact with a crafted log file. Microsoft is currently investigating the report and notes that Defender can detect exploitation attempts, though no official patch has been released.

items.title: LLMON: An LLM-Native Markup Language, now in Granite 4.1 3B and 8B
items.one_liner: LLMON is an XML-like markup language designed to defeat prompt injection and replace brittle JSON parsing in LLMs.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced LLMON (LLM Object Notation), an LLM-native markup language designed to replace JSON for causal language models by using reserved special-token delimiters for explicit structure and data binding. By wrapping semantic components in tags and mapping unique identifiers to instructions, the format prevents indirect prompt injections and stops models from pulling unrelated context into answers. IBM has released two experimental preview models based on Granite 4.1 (3B and 8B parameters) trained natively on LLMON, alongside a GitHub toolkit for conversions and workflows.
items.bottom_line: Adopting LLMON and its supporting Granite models eliminates indirect prompt injection risks by explicitly binding instructions to data payloads.

items.bottom_line: Wiki.js installations must update to version 2.5.315 to eliminate dangerous Vue directive whitelisting and prevent cross-site scripting attacks.

items.one_liner: CVE-2026-129490 exposes a stack out-of-bounds read in littlefs during version 1 image migration, causing potential crashes.
items.summary: A type confusion and stack out-of-bounds read vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-129490 with a CVSS score of 5.5, has been discovered in littlefs up to version v2.11.3 when built with LFS_MIGRATE. items.title: CVE-2026-115690: Apache WSS4J: Replay protection bypassed by concurrent copies of a message
items.one_liner: A race condition in Apache WSS4J replay protection allows concurrent requests to bypass checks and execute multiple times unless updated.
items.summary: Apache WSS4J suffers from a replay protection bypass vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-115690, affecting versions 4.0.0 prior to 4.0.3, 3.0.0 prior to 3.0.7, and versions before 2.4.5. The library previously checked whether a message's UsernameToken Nonce, timestamp, signature, or SAML assertion ID had been seen before validating the message, treating the check and record phases as separate steps. Concurrent processing of identical message copies allowed them to bypass the check simultaneously and execute multiple times. The vulnerability is resolved by updating the logic to check and record values in a single atomic step using ReplayCache.addIfAbsent.
key_facts: Affected versions: Apache WSS4J 4.0.0 before 4.0.3, 3.0.0 before 3.0.7, and before 2.4.5
items.bottom_line: Deployments using Apache WSS4J must upgrade to versions 4.0.3, 3.0.7, or 2.4.5 to enforce atomic replay caching and prevent message duplication attacks.

claims.text: Apache WSS4J remembers the UsernameToken Nonce, the Timestamp and signature of a signed message, and the ID of a SAML 2.0 "OneTimeUse" assertion, so that a captured message cannot be accepted twice.

items.title: How I Found a $113,337 AF_ALG Linux Local Privilege Escalation Before Copy Fail
items.one_liner: A retrospective look at uncovering a $113,337 Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw in the AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem via unprivileged socket APIs.
items.summary: Security researcher Muhammad Alifa Ramdhan details the discovery of CVE-2025-39964, a critical race condition vulnerability in the Linux kernel's AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem that earned a $113,337 reward via Google's kernelCTF. Exploiting out-of-bounds access stemming from how AF_ALG handles inputs across unprivileged sockets, an ordinary user can escalate privileges to root or achieve container escape. Present in the kernel since 2011, this vulnerability preceded the widely known 'Copy Fail' flaw but highlights the same underlying kernel attack surface.
items.bottom_line: Unprivileged access to the Linux kernel's AF_ALG subsystem harbors deep race condition vulnerabilities capable of full privilege escalation and container escape.

items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has established a specialized sub-group under its Primary Market Advisory Committee to review regulations governing public fundraisings such as IPOs, FPOs, and QIPs. The panel will examine issuer eligibility criteria, lock-in periods, pricing frameworks, and disclosure norms to eliminate duplication and streamline capital access. This initiative follows SEBI's broader review of SME listing frameworks, which proposed raising minimum operating profit requirements and adjusting post-issue market capitalization thresholds. The comprehensive regulatory review aims to modernize India's primary market compliance requirements ahead of the upcoming Union budget.
key_facts: Advisory committee: Primary Market Advisory Committee (PMAC)
Regulations under review: SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018
items.bottom_line: SEBI has constituted a PMAC sub-group to review and rationalize ICDR regulations for IPOs, FPOs, and QIPs to improve market access.

items.title: When One GPU Isn’t Enough: Serving GLM-5.3 Across Two NVIDIA DGX Stations with vLLM
items.one_liner: A practical guide for deploying massive MoE models across multi-node GPU clusters using vLLM and RDMA.
items.summary: This technical guide details how to serve the 753-billion-parameter GLM-5.3 model across two NVIDIA DGX Stations using vLLM. Because the model's 464 GB checkpoint exceeds the 252 GB HBM3e capacity of a single GB300 GPU, tensor parallelism is used to split weights across two connected stations. The setup utilizes ConnectX-8 RDMA for high-speed communication between the nodes. The tutorial covers the configuration of Docker, network settings, and the deployment of the model as an OpenAI-compatible API endpoint.
items.bottom_line: Scaling frontier-scale models locally requires multi-node tensor parallelism and high-bandwidth interconnects to overcome single-GPU memory limitations.
